name: DTiX ITcenter Chevigny-Saint-Sauveur
notes: Colocation DC in the Dijon agglomeration (Chevigny-Saint-Sauveur), delivered Q2 2020: 120 racks in 3 rooms, 450 m2 IT space, Tier III, PUE<1.5 free-cooling. Regional business press (La Gazette Bourgogne/Aletheia Press).

name: Périgord Numérique proximity data center
developer: Syndicat mixte Périgord numérique (SMPN), supported by Département de la Dordogne
notes: First local/proximity data center project in Dordogne led by SMPN; status per regional business press, no permit/environmental filing verified yet.

name: nLighten Edge Besançon
notes: nLighten edge/colo data center in Besançon; operator official page lists the facility as active edge site; capacity not disclosed.

name: Sesterce AI supercomputer campus (Rovaltain/Alixan)
notes: AI supercomputer/datacenter campus at Rovaltain near Valence TGV (Alixan). Permit for 40 MW (expandable to 80 MW) granted Dec 2025 by Alixan mayor; suspended 10 Jul 2026 by tribunal administratif de Grenoble for missing environmental impact study; Sesterce seeking 'Projet d'Intérêt National' status. 40,000 GPUs planned, ~EUR 1.5bn. Status blocked pending appeal; do not count as active construction.

name: DATA4 Paris-Saclay campus PAR01/PAR02 (Marcoussis)
notes: DATA4 historical Paris-Saclay campus at Marcoussis (PAR01) and Nozay (PAR02), carrier-neutral colo; part of 500 MW Marcoussis-Nozay pole ambition.

name: DATA4 PAR03 AI campus (Nozay)
notes: New 22-hectare DATA4 campus at Nozay (Paris-Saclay territory), construction launch announced; part of plan to build Europe's largest digital hub (500 MW on the Marcoussis-Nozay pole, marketing figure).

name: Eclairion Bruyères-le-Châtel (Mistral AI cluster)
notes: Modular high-density AI data center on 4-ha site in Bruyères-le-Châtel (~30-40 km south of Paris), hosting Mistral AI first cluster: 13,800 Nvidia GB300 GPUs, ~44 MW installed (60 MW per aggregator). Entered operational phase 2026; EUR 50m raise reported by DCD.

name: Orange datacenter campus Val-de-Reuil (Normandie 1 & 2)
notes: Orange's giant Normandy cloud campus in the Eure (Val-de-Reuil): first building (Normandie 1) ~2014 (~EUR 100m), second (Normandie 2) 16,000 m2 building / 5,000 m2 IT rooms with free cooling; both operational.

name: Orange data center Amilly
notes: Orange data center at Amilly (near Chartres, Eure-et-Loir), ~EUR 50m investment, in operation end-2020, replica of Val-de-Reuil Normandie 2 with free cooling; '50 GW' figure in article is a typo, capacity not established.

name: Pebsco data center Brest
notes: Small (~EUR 1m) local data center project in Brest by Pebsco (regional business press); site/status not re-verified; treat as announced lead.

name: Auch local data center (Apexi / Fullsave)
notes: Local data center project in Auch announced for 2022 to host local digital data; current operational status unverified (regional press).

name: Equinix BX1 Bordeaux (Bruges)
notes: Equinix BX1 at Bruges (Bordeaux Metropole), 3,000 m2, operational since 2021; Equinix's 10th French site and first outside Ile-de-France.

name: BXIA AI supercomputer & data center (Bordeaux-Lac)
notes: EUR 3bn AI supercomputer/data center project at Bordeaux-Lac (20-ha former parking site), ~380 MW electrical power planned by 2040; Bordeaux Metropole gave green light 30 Jan 2026; replaces abandoned Equinix BX2 project; environmental engagements incl. heat reuse and renaturation.

name: Cheops Technology data center Canéjan
notes: Tier III-class facility at Canéjan near Bordeaux per aggregator DataCenterMap; capacity unverified.
